## Purpose and Entrypoint
Micro is a cross-platform, terminal-based text editor distributed as a largely self-contained Go binary. The executable entrypoint is `cmd/micro/micro.go`; startup/setup support and Lua initialization are in `cmd/micro/initlua.go` and `cmd/micro/clean.go`. Invocation opens files or stdin into editor buffers.

## Startup, Runtime Assets, and Configuration
Startup loads embedded/bundled runtime content, user configuration, settings, colorschemes, plugins, and defaults before entering the interactive editor loop. Runtime discovery and configuration ownership sit in `internal/config/config.go`, `internal/config/rtfiles.go`, and `runtime/runtime.go`. The `runtime/` tree supplies help, syntax definitions, Lua plugins, and themes rather than requiring external application services.

## Editor State and Text Model
`internal/buffer` is the core mutable document layer: buffers hold text, cursor-related state, settings, undo/redo history, search, serialization, backups, and save behavior. Primary files are `internal/buffer/buffer.go`, `internal/buffer/eventhandler.go`, and `internal/buffer/save.go`. Editing actions should cross this boundary through buffer/event abstractions so undo, persistence, and multi-cursor semantics remain coherent.

## Interaction and Command Dispatch
`internal/action` coordinates keyboard/mouse events, commands, panes, tabs, and editor-global state. Keybindings are resolved through `internal/action/bindings.go` and `internal/action/keytree.go`; commands and action execution live in `internal/action/command.go` and `internal/action/actions.go`. This layer maps terminal input into mutations of buffers and view/layout state, and is the main control-plane boundary for user-facing features.

## Views, Rendering, and Terminal Boundary
The UI is a terminal renderer, not a web application. `internal/views/splits.go` manages split layout; `internal/display/bufwindow.go`, `internal/display/statusline.go`, and related display windows render panes and metadata. `internal/screen/screen.go` abstracts terminal screen operations. Terminal capability, raw input, mouse support, and color behavior are constrained by the Go/tcell terminal environment.

## Extensibility and External Integration
Lua is the plugin extension boundary: `internal/lua/lua.go` hosts Lua, while `internal/config/plugin.go` and `internal/config/plugin_manager.go` manage plugin lifecycle/install behavior. Built-in Lua plugins reside under `runtime/plugins/`. Shell jobs and embedded terminals are mediated by `internal/shell/job.go` and `internal/shell/terminal.go`. Clipboard integration uses platform/system tools where available, behind `internal/clipboard/clipboard.go` and `internal/clipboard/terminal.go`.

## Syntax and Distribution
Syntax highlighting is a reusable package plus declarative language definitions: `pkg/highlight/highlighter.go`, `pkg/highlight/parser.go`, and `runtime/syntax/`. Color themes are loaded from `runtime/colorschemes/`. Build/release infrastructure produces static-oriented binaries and platform packages through `Makefile`, `tools/cross-compile.sh`, and `snapcraft.yaml`; GitHub Actions workflows drive test, nightly, and release automation.
